title: Care at Capacity
briefing: Heat-related illness and the water alert have filled the regional hospitals. A new intake surge is expected overnight. Beds, staff, transport and backup equipment cannot all be expanded at once. The team must decide where to concentrate the next shift’s care capacity.

private_intelligence.infrastructure: A convention hall can support temporary wards, but its cooling must be connected to hospital reserve circuits. Transfers avoid that retrofit and let maintenance crews repair those circuits tonight.
private_intelligence.community: Patients’ families are already sharing stories of transfers without notice. Nearby care would reassure them; postponing routine appointments is more acceptable if the rescheduling commitment is credible.
private_intelligence.economy: A staffed temporary ward uses nearly a week of the emergency purchasing reserve. Transfers have a reimbursement agreement, while a planned-care pause sacrifices revenue but releases experienced staff.
private_intelligence.safety: Two partner hospitals report spare beds, yet the transfer route averages 95 minutes and ambulances lack enough critical-care escorts. Temporary wards can handle observation, not complex surgery.

choices.title: Open Temporary Care Wards
choices.description: Equip the convention hall for staffed observation and divert hospital reserve utilities to support it.
choices.consequence: Nearby beds reduce immediate harm and reassure families. Rapid utility conversion strains essential systems, and staffing plus equipment purchases deplete financial reserves.

choices.title: Transfer to Regional Partners
choices.description: Use the reimbursement agreement and move suitable patients to hospitals outside the city.
choices.consequence: Local utility repairs and reimbursement strengthen systems and finances. Lengthy transfers delay treatment and distress families, increasing health risks and mistrust.

choices.title: Pause Planned Care
choices.description: Suspend scheduled care, redeploy staff, and publish a protected rescheduling programme.
choices.consequence: Staff redeployment allows orderly maintenance and a transparent plan improves confidence. Lost treatment revenue weakens finances, while deferred care creates avoidable health complications.
